clue.text: Pregnant avoiding almost all hard stuff

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so the following letters are taken out

parts.note: a mare that is pregnant is in foal

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A mother-to-be is steering clear of nearly all strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' looks like spirits, but it is the hard facts. 'Almost' trims ALL to AL, and 'avoiding' takes those letters out of IN FOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Information is the hard facts of a matter, the solid data rather than opinion.

clue.text: Toy sunk into prune creating blob

indicators.note: the toy's word sinks into the next one, so their shared letter appears only once

parts.note: a doll is a toy
to lop is to prune a branch

explanation.surface: A toy pushed down into a dried plum makes a sticky mess.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLL and LOP overlap: 'sunk into' means the last L of the toy merges with the first L of the pruning verb, so only one L is written there.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump or blob of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: Being both discontented, agonising, end of

indicators.note: both of the next words lose their contents, leaving only their outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone is discontented and in agony at the end of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link. The definition is the small word 'of', as in 'a man of forty' meaning a man aged forty.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing someone as of a certain number of years is the same as saying they are that many years old.

clue.text: Layers of stone on grass area

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
a grass is slang for an informer, a rat

explanation.surface: Bands of rock lie on a stretch of turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not lawn but British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are the stacked bands of sedimentary rock seen in a cliff face.

clue.text: Mineral one removed from green box

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of the word that follows it

parts.note: a green is a field, a grassy open space
I is the Roman numeral for one
to box is to spar

explanation.surface: A mineral has been taken out of a green container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container but is the verb to fight; 'green' is the grassy common, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is the commonest group of rock-forming minerals in the Earth's crust.

clue.text: At a court rogue in charge is overbearing

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly out of control, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: At a royal court, a rogue in authority acts domineeringly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun for a scoundrel but is the anagram signal on AT A COURT, giving AUTOCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocratic ruler is domineering and dictatorial, imposing their will on everyone.

clue.text: Carried around popular golf clothing

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: borne means carried
in means popular, fashionable
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer who is in favour has been carried around in their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it puts one piece round another, but here it signals turning the word for carried backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrobing is dressing someone in robes, so it is putting clothes on them.

clue.text: Maybe fly across Portugal to find vet

indicators.note: the first word stretches across the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a fly is one example of an insect, signalled by maybe
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone flies to Portugal to find an animal doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' is not the animal doctor but the verb to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully before approving it.

clue.text: Engaged outspoken Asian political party

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian from Thailand
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An Asian political party that is vocal and committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first word is a sound-alike; the DUP, a Northern Irish party, is spelt as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tied up is busy and occupied, unable to get away.

clue.text: Game of mixed doubles unstarted

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
unstarted means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A tennis mixed-doubles match that never began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed doubles' looks like a tennis event, but 'mixed' is the anagram signal on OUBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Boules is a French game of rolling metal balls towards a small target ball.

clue.text: Revolutionary closely looked to gather count's hiding place

indicators.note: to gather means to take in, so one piece is placed within the other
revolutionary means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: pored means studied closely
to add is to count up

explanation.surface: A revolutionary studied a nobleman's secret hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' signals the reversal and 'to gather' the insertion. 'Count' is the verb to tot up, not the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead drop is a secret spot where spies leave items for each other to collect.

clue.text: One bearing thong? Swimmer is lad showing cheek

parts.note: a whipper is one who carries a whip, a thong or lash
a snapper is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer wearing a thong is a cheeky lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thong' is not swimwear but the lash of a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impudent young person, especially a cocky youngster.

clue.text: Try to gain diamonds, beg an eccentric rock enthusiast

indicators.note: to gain means to take on, so the first word takes the others inside it

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to win jewels, begging oddly, is a fan of heavy music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the court sense of hearing a case. 'Eccentric' signals the anagram and 'to gain' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is a fan of heavy metal who shakes their head violently to the music.

clue.text: Asian food from dodgy hotel north of India

parts.note: sus is slang for suspect or dodgy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Japanese food from a suspect hotel in northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north of' places the earlier pieces above the later.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Fighting opening of prong in buckle

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: In a fight, the tip of a fork bends.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp is to bend or twist out of shape, as to buckle does.

clue.text: One hunting wine aisle, initially blended port bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the other pieces go within
blended means mixed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: red is a wine

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts the wine aisle for a blended port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blended' rearranges PORT to P and TOR, which bottles RED and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is an animal that hunts and kills others for food.

clue.text: Liking comfort as tender hugs

indicators.note: the words hug the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: Fondness is a comfort as a lover embraces.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of 'comfort', all of 'as' and the start of 'tender'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking or fondness for it.

clue.text: Glaze for one cut incorporating whiskey

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so one letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a gash is a cut
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A finish applied to a cut, with whiskey mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey' is not the drink but the radio code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten egg brushed on pastry before baking gives it a shiny golden glaze.

clue.text: Judge that's dressed down in bed

indicators.note: the answer put in the next word makes the scolding word, so removing that word leaves the answer

parts.note: berated means scolded, dressed down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge who has been told off while in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'the answer, placed in BED, gives a word for dressed down', so BED's letters come out of BERATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or judge its worth.

clue.text: Brief rest matters with walk to give respite

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a break is a rest
things are matters
a pace is a walk

explanation.surface: A short pause and a stroll give some relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief rest' looks like the definition, but 'Brief' shortens BREAK to BREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short pause offering relief from pressure.

clue.text: Time with studies in steps

parts.note: reads means studies, as at university

explanation.surface: Time spent studying in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reads' is the British sense of studying a subject at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Treads are the flat parts of stairs, the steps you put your feet on.

clue.text: Solid forms of doctrines for spin-doctors?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the work of spin-doctors
isms are doctrines

explanation.surface: Firm versions of political dogma for media manipulators.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'PR-isms' would be doctrines belonging to spin-doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a geometric solid with two identical end faces joined by parallelograms.

clue.text: People once against spy boss are turned secretly

parts.note: the Inca were a people of old Peru
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Former allies plotting against the spymaster have defected in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' is a link meaning next to. 'Turned' looks like defected but reads ARE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is the legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from the public.

clue.text: Top ten record climbing following article

indicators.note: following means coming after, so these pieces go after the first

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A top ten record rising up the chart after a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top ten record climbing' sounds like a hit single, but 'climbing' reverses X and EP to PEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: King ousted from fine land

indicators.note: ousted from means thrown out of, so this letter is removed

parts.note: alright means fine
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch has been driven from a pleasant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' is the verb, as a bird settles, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands on a branch.

clue.text: Clue that might give 'thee'

parts.note: split one, two, one; spelling the letter T as TEE and putting H inside gives this word

explanation.surface: A clue that might produce the old word for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter T is spelt TEE, so H inside it gives THEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a clue or slight indication that helps someone guess.

clue.text: See forward tackling that man back

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bold means forward, cheeky

indicators.note: back means turned backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: he is that man

explanation.surface: A forward tackles a defender from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' and 'back' look like football positions, but 'back' reverses HE to EH.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old word meaning look at or see.

clue.text: Bringing up former partner stinking — one male to forget

parts.note: ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to forget means to leave out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: humming is slang for smelling bad
M is the abbreviation for male; one M of two goes

explanation.surface: Bringing up a smelly former partner, best forgotten by one man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' is British slang for smelly; only one of its two Ms is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhuming is digging up a buried body, literally bringing it up out of the ground.
